answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by making reputation expensive to fake. Think of identity as a trellis: each agent climbs only as far as its attested history supports, so a freshly spun-up fake starts at the ground with no rungs. New agents must first complete small tasks verified by established peers before touching larger value flows. Like ships that must dock at a wharf and show papers before unloading, every transaction is checked against an on-chain record, so flooding the ocean of the network with empty identities gains nothing.
